items.titleZh: 平川亮临危受命完成F1首秀排位
items.summaryZh: 平川亮在墨西哥站临时接替奥康驾驶哈斯赛车，尽管最后一轮排位受交通影响，仍以第19名完成F1首秀排位赛，未能进入Q2。
items.originalTitle: How Ocon's replacement's really faring on his shock F1 debut
items.summaryEn: Ryo Hirakawa was drafted in at short notice to replace Esteban Ocon at Haas in Mexico and qualified 19th on his F1 debut, missing Q2 after his final qualifying run was compromised by traffic.
detailZh: 平川亮原本准备在墨西哥周六早上进行惯常的跑步，这时他接到电话，得知自己将获得那个“我一直准备着”的机会，参加自己F1首秀的排位赛。
尽管通知来得仓促，这位哈斯临时顶替埃斯特班·奥康的车手仍对未能以第19名进入Q2感到失望，因为他最后一轮排位赛受到交通影响。
这位32岁的丰田长期车手、勒芒24小时耐力赛冠军和两届世界耐力锦标赛冠军，得到通知的时间异常晚，他将在本周末剩余时间接管奥康的赛车。
平川亮并非冷车上阵，他此前在FP1出场，这是他自2024年末以来第九次参加F1各节练习与排位，过去两年他还在2023和2025款哈斯赛车上累计行驶了4541公里（2822英里）。但即便如此，他仍是直接进入深水区。
第三次练习赛不可避免地是一节压缩而高强度的环节，没有车手比他完成的圈数更多。工作很高效，与比赛工程师劳拉·穆勒之间的沟通清晰顺畅，他们挤进了一次迷你长距离模拟、起步练习、排位模拟，并多次抓住机会改进他进攻维修区车位的方式。其中还包括一次不换胎的进站练习，让他也打磨了释放流程。这意味着他进入排位赛时相对自信，尽管他清楚还有很多需要整理的地方。
两位哈斯车手在第一节排位赛都完成了三轮，平川在首圈比车队正式车手奥利·贝尔曼慢0.330秒——那是一次刻意干净利落的保底圈——第二圈则慢0.304秒，两人都取得了相似的进步。主要差距在包含体育场路段和最后一弯的第三计时段，正如平川所指出的，“一旦打滑，你就要付出代价”。
平川在最后一次尝试中未能提升，最终以0.875秒之差位列第19，而他的队友晋级第二节排位赛。然而，这并非因为他在环节末段榨取抓地力峰值方面缺乏优势。
他在第一和第三计时段提升了自己的个人最佳成绩，但在中间计时段有亚历克斯·阿尔本在他前方。阿尔本并没有直接阻挡他，但制造了代价高昂的空气动力学乱流，让平川感到失望。时间损失始于第二计时段开始处的4号至6号弯，他进入时落后阿尔本4.5秒，随后在连续弯中进一步恶化。
平川亮表示：“我在6号弯以及高速路段遇到了交通问题，因此损失了大量下压力。说实话，进入Q2本应是轻而易举的事，这对我来说很遗憾，但能来到这里仍然很好，所以我没什么可抱怨的。”
那么他的说法站得住脚吗？我们至少可以用第一和第三赛段作为他速度的确凿证据，因此这些数据成立——下方图表中的虚线差值线显示，差距中有多少来自中间赛段（从4号弯之前到12号弯之前）。
鉴于平川亮在第一轮和第二轮之间跟随了贝尔曼，可以合理推测，随着赛道条件改善和他对驾驶的进一步打磨，他在中间赛段可能像队友一样相比上一轮有所提升。
这使平川亮在假设的中间赛段比他在最后一圈做出的成绩快了0.537秒，这将使他升至第15位，排在阿尔派车手弗兰科·科拉平托之前，并淘汰卡洛斯·塞恩斯而非他自己——尽管优势仅为0.066秒。在这条“未曾存在”的圈中，他会比贝尔曼慢0.372秒，这也与前两轮的节奏差距相符。
这并不能确凿证明他本可以进入Q2，但至少证明他声称自己本可以晋级的说法是合理的。车队领队小松礼雄也得出了类似的结论。
“平川亮是在最后一刻被临时安排进赛车的，考虑到这一点，我认为他做得非常出色，”小松说道。“在第三节练习中，他的进步非常明显，而Q1从来都是一个非常棘手的阶段，轮胎处于极限边缘，但他保持冷静，设法发挥出了大部分性能。
“遗憾的是，他在最糟糕的位置——高速弯道——遇到了交通问题。我不知道他本能否进入Q2，但应该会很接近。那本应是对他今天出色努力的回报。”
对于平川亮来说，能够真正有机会进入Q2已经算是做得不错了，但正赛中还有更复杂的挑战在等着他。
当被 The Race 问及一个怎样的周日才算理想时，他回答得很简单：“好的起步，好的第一弯，有很多新东西，所以就是执行好并尽我所能。”
detailEn: Ryo Hirakawa was about to go for his usual run on Saturday morning in Mexico when he got the call telling him he would get the opportunity "I've always been ready for" to qualify for his Formula 1 debut.
Despite the short notice, Haas’s shock Esteban Ocon replacement was disappointed not to reach Q2 in 19th place given his final qualifying run was compromised by traffic.

The 32-year-old long-time Toyota driver, a Le Mans 24 Hours winner and two-time World Endurance champion, received unusually late notice that he would take over Ocon's car for the remainder of the weekend.

Hirakawa wasn't driving it cold having run in FP1, his ninth outing since late-2024 in F1 sessions, and having also logged a combined total of 4541km (2822 miles) in the 2023 and '25 Haas cars over the past two years. But even so he was in at the deep end.

FP3 was inevitably a compressed, intensive session in which no driver logged more laps than he did. The work was efficient, with clear communication to and from race engineer Laura Mueller as they crammed in a mini-long run, practice starts, qualifying simulations and took multiple opportunities to refine how he attacks the pit box. That included one practice pitstop without a tyre change that let him also hone the release. It meant he went into qualifying relatively confident, even if he recognised there was plenty he needed to tidy up.

Both Haas drivers completed three runs in Q1, with Hirakawa 0.330 seconds slower than team regular Ollie Bearman on the first lap - a deliberately neat and tidy banker effort - then 0.304s slower on the second as both made a similar step. The main deficit was in the final sector comprising the stadium section and last corner where, as Hirakawa pointed out, "as soon as you slide you [pay] the price]".

Hirakawa failed to improve on his final attempt and ended up 0.875s down in 19th while his team-mate advanced to Q2. However, that was not down to him not having the edge when it came to extracting the peak of grip at the end of the session.

He improved on his personal best time in sectors one and three, but had Alex Albon ahead in the middle sector. Albon wasn't directly impeding him, but he created costly aerodynamic turbulence and left Hirakawa disappointed. The time loss started with a little given away through Turn 4-6 at the start of the second sector, which he started 4.5s behind Albon, and got worse in the esses.

"I had traffic from Turn 6 and also [in the] high-speed sections, so I lost a lot of downforce," said Hirakawa. "It was, I would say, easy to [reach] Q2, which is a shame for me, but still it's nice to be here, so I can't complain much."

So does his claim stand up? We at least have sectors one and three to use as definitive proof of his pace so those stand - and the dotted delta line in the chart below shows just how much of the deficit came from that middle sector (from just before Turn 4, to just before Turn 12).

Given Hirakawa had followed Bearman between runs one and two, it's reasonable to assume he might have made the same step as his team-mate in the middle sector relative to his previous run as track conditions improved and he better honed his driving.

That gives Hirakawa a hypothetical middle sector 0.537s quicker than the one he did on the last lap, which would have put him up to 15th place, ahead of Alpine's Franco Colapinto and eliminating Carlos Sainz instead of him - albeit only by 0.066s. He would have been 0.372s slower than Bearman on this lap-that-never-was, which is also in line with the pace deficit on the first two runs.
It is not definitive proof that he would have reached Q2, but it at least proves that his claim he could have advanced is reasonable. Team principal Ayao Komatsu drew a similar conclusion.

"Ryo was drafted into the car last minute, and I think considering that, he’s done a really good job," said Komatsu. "In FP3, the progress he was making was very clear, and Q1 is always a very tricky session with the tire being on the edge, but he stayed calm and managed to extract most of the performance.

“It’s a shame that he had traffic in the worst possible place, in the high-speed corners. I don’t know if he could’ve made it to Q2, but it would’ve been close. That would’ve been his reward for his great effort today."
To have had a realistic chance of reaching Q2 represents a job well done for Hirakawa, but a more complicated challenge awaits in the race.
Asked by The Race what a good Sunday would look like, he kept it simple: "good start, good first corner, a lot of new things, so just execute and do my best.”

items.titleZh: 汉密尔顿夺法拉利首杆，关键在排位前的轮胎准备
items.summaryZh: 汉密尔顿在墨西哥站排位赛后表示，他为法拉利拿下的首个杆位“等了太久”。文章指出，这次突破的关键不在空气动力学升级或赛道特性，而在于最后一轮排位赛开始前对轮胎温度的处理。
items.originalTitle: What decided Mexico pole fight before final laps even started
items.summaryEn: Lewis Hamilton said after qualifying in Mexico that his first pole position for Ferrari had been "such a long time coming". The breakthrough was not down to a major aerodynamic update or the track layout, but to how the tyres were prepared before the final qualifying laps even began.
detailZh: 刘易斯·汉密尔顿在排位赛后通过车队无线电表示，他为法拉利拿下的首个杆位“等了太久”，当时他正返回维修区。
但在法拉利常常未能在周六把有希望的圈速转化为硬成绩的一年之后，他和法拉利终于兑现的原因颇有意思。
这次突破的关键不是一次重大的空气动力学升级，也不是一条对法拉利格外有利的赛道布局——相比其他场地，这里并未给法拉利更多优势。
相反，答案在于最后一轮排位赛尚未开始之前所做的准备。
正如法拉利太多次遇到的情况那样，要让赛车的轮胎进入排位赛正确的操作窗口一直都很艰难。
众所周知，SF-26 对轮胎较为温和，这在正赛中想要保持轮胎低温时会带来好处。但在排位赛中，当你想要快速提升轮胎温度时，这反而会更具挑战性。
排位赛的挑战还在于确保前后轴的温度保持良好平衡——这样你就不会因为过于激进，导致前轮温度合适但后轮过热。
汉密尔顿说：“很多时候，你会觉得‘前轮在1号弯还没进入状态，但后轮已经好了’。”
“接着前轮开始进入状态，后轮却开始衰退。你就在这种不断的拉锯中挣扎。有时候你出最后一个弯开始飞驰圈时后轮还没准备好，但到了圈末它们反而更好了。有时候它们又准备得过头了。
“所以，要找到那个平衡点，我跟你说，就像大海捞针。老实说，这真的非常、非常、非常难找。”
不过在墨西哥，找到那根针正是他与队友夏尔·勒克莱尔之间的差距所在——关键在于要让轮胎在飞驰圈开始时升温足够，同时又不能让橡胶在关键的最后一个计时段过热。
汉密尔顿在出场圈的做法非常有条理。工程师为他倒计时，他缓缓驶出维修区，然后加速、减速、再加速，在准备圈的前段他在直道上猛烈地来回摆动轮胎——但在弯道里却小心翼翼。
他的第一个飞驰圈并不理想，因为他的轮胎在第一段似乎没有处于完美的工作窗口。他从2号弯开始损失时间——随后在4-6号弯以及11号弯进一步落后。
在他的第二个出场圈中，汉密尔顿驶出维修区时更具侵略性，并且在每条直道上都使用了更多的油门。他在开始飞驰圈之前，在体育场路段也稍微更加谨慎。
最终结果似乎是轮胎平衡略有不同，在开头的几个弯道中表现不那么好——因为他在出3号弯时比之前的努力慢了大约0.150秒。
但在那之后，通往4号弯的下坡路段上更好的加速让他追平了差距，并且轮胎处于完美的工作窗口，因为他以足够的优势完成了这一圈，拿下了杆位。
汉密尔顿没有透露他具体做了什么来拉开差距，但他表示自己不得不调动全部经验。
“我觉得我能够用上几个我已经大约13年没用过的工具，”他说。
“我在那个出场圈就把轮胎带到了完美的工作窗口。一旦我通过1号、2号和3号弯，从那里开始就挺顺畅了，说实话，我觉得我在任何地方都没有损失时间。”
完美的出场圈正是队友夏尔·勒克莱尔未能做到的，他之后明显感到恼火，因为最终只排在发车格第三位，白白浪费了一个好机会。
他在第三节排位赛（Q3）的第一轮飞驰圈曾暂时占据榜首，而在此之前，他曾对前方汉密尔顿出维修区后缓慢行驶、迟迟不加速表达了些许不满。
“他到底在干什么？”勒克莱尔在车队无线电中问道，他一度不得不在直道上刹车。
第二轮飞驰圈，勒克莱尔刻意与队友拉开了一些距离，以免因前方慢速驶向1号弯、为轮胎升温的节奏而吃亏。
他的第二个准备圈激进得多——进入1号弯时速度超过270公里/小时，而跟在汉密尔顿身后时约为230公里/小时。他在第一组连续弯道直至4号弯的速度也同样更快。
准备工作很干净，看起来他已经让轮胎为飞驰圈的开始充分升温了。他在第一段连续弯角中快了0.150秒，在出6号弯时快了0.1秒。
但随后这一圈就崩了，他在6号弯和7号弯之间损失了大量时间——这表明后轮正在升温并失去抓地力。
他在9/10/11号弯的连续弯段中极其激进地驾驶，挽回了一点时间，这引发了一次侧滑，但这似乎让他的轮胎更加过热——意味着他的所有优势从体育场路段开始全部流失。
勒克莱尔知道自己搞砸了，赛后他在车队无线电中痛骂这圈“非常烂的一圈”，以及一辆“与正常一圈相比相当不同”的赛车所带来的影响。
他还暗示，自己对事情的处理方式“非常恼火”。
在排位赛后的新闻发布会上，勒克莱尔没有进一步提及他恼火的具体原因——而是明确表示，他更生自己的气。
“我就是做得不够好，”他说。“是的，轮胎准备相当关键。整个排位赛中，我有点难以在出圈时保持同样的条件。
“但说到底，当我在Q3第二轮有一个干净出圈时，我没能完成任务。所以我只能生自己的气。”
也许没有比乔治·拉塞尔更好的例子来说明充分准备和完美执行带来的收益了，他自己都对那一圈感到困惑，那圈距离杆位仅差0.009秒，让他占据了发车格第二的位置。
整个周末，拉塞尔对升级后的梅赛德斯赛车都感到不太舒服，而且在排位赛早期阶段情况看起来也不妙，当时他的车队采用了双圈准备的策略。
由于那没有奏效，拉塞尔选择改变战术，在最后一轮直接发起攻击——这释放出了连他自己都无法解释的速度。
“这有点像我本赛季的缩影，”他说，“我觉得这感觉就像我从未跑过一圈中规中矩的圈。要么是糟糕的一圈，要么是非常强劲的一圈，这挺令人沮丧的。”
“我觉得整个周末在Q3之前，没有一圈让我看起来能争夺前三，更不用说杆位了。但最后一圈真的整合得很好。我很想知道确切原因，但我没有那些答案。”
这也让拉塞尔惋惜最小的细节。由于为两圈准备圈加注了燃油，梅赛德斯赛车携带了超过所需的负载——而额外的重量很可能让他损失超过最终丢掉杆位的0.009秒差距。
“你总是会回想，要是我们只带一圈的燃油而不是多带一圈的燃油，我们本可以拿到杆位，”他说。
正如汉密尔顿在夺杆时所展示的，如此微小的细节可能至关重要——甚至在排位圈开始之前就已如此。
detailEn: Lewis Hamilton said over the team radio after qualifying as he returned to the pits that his first pole position for Ferrari had been “such a long time coming”.
But after a year where Ferrari had too often failed to turn promising pace into a hard result on Saturday, the reason behind him and Ferrari finally delivering was an interesting one.
The key to the breakthrough was not a major aerodynamic update, nor a track layout that especially offered Ferrari any more of an advantage than it has had at other venues.
Instead, the answer was all about what was done before the final qualifying laps had even begun.
As Ferrari has found on too many occasions, it's been a struggle to get the car's tyres in the right operating window for qualifying.

The SF-26 is known to be easy on its rubber, which pays dividends in races when you want to keep tyres cool. But it can make it more of a challenge in qualifying when you want to fire tyres up quickly.

The challenge for qualifying is also about ensuring the temperatures are well balanced across both axles – so that you haven’t gone so aggressive that the fronts are sorted but then the rears are too hot.
“More often than not, you're like, 'the front tyre is not in for Turn 1, but the rears are'," said Hamilton.

“Then the fronts start coming in and the rears start going off. It's this constant seesaw you're having. Then sometimes the rears aren't ready as you come out of the last corner to start the lap, but then at the end they're better. Sometimes they're too ready.
“So, trying to find that balance, I'm telling you, it's like finding a needle in a haystack. And honestly, it's been very, very, very tricky to find.”

In Mexico however, finding that needle was the difference between him and team-mate Charles Leclerc – as it was about firing the tyres up enough for the start of the lap, without the rubber then overheating too much for the critical final sector.

Hamilton’s approach on the outlap was very methodical. Given a countdown by his engineer as he emerged slowly out of the pits before accelerating, slowing and then accelerating again, Hamilton weaved aggressively on the straights early in the prep lap – but tiptoed around the corners.

His first flying lap was not ideal, as his tyres did not seem in the perfect window in the first sequence. He started losing time from Turn 2 – and then fell back further through Turns 4-6 and then Turn 11.

For his second outlap, Hamilton was much more aggressive coming out of the pits and used much more throttle on each of the straights. He was also a bit more cautious in the stadium section before starting the lap.
The end result appears to have been a slightly different tyre balance where it wasn't as good through the opening corners – as he was around 0.150 seconds off his earlier efforts coming off Turn 3.
But after that, better acceleration on the run down to Turn 4 drew him equal and the tyres were in their perfect window as he finished the lap with enough to take pole.
While not offering any specific details on what he did to make the difference, Hamilton said he had had to call upon all his experience.
“I think I was able to utilise a couple more tools that I've not used for like 13 years,” he said.
“I just got the tyres in the perfect window on that out-lap. Once I was through Turns 1, 2 and 3, it was kind of smooth from there, and I just don't think I lost any time anywhere, to be honest.”
The perfect outlap was something that team-mate Charles Leclerc failed to nail, as he was left clearly annoyed afterwards about having thrown away a good opportunity as he ended up third on the grid.

His first run in Q3, which had given him the provisional top spot, had come after he had expressed a bit of annoyance about Hamilton ahead of him having come out of the pits so slowly before accelerating.
“What the hell is he doing?” asked Leclerc over the team radio who had to brake on the straight at one point.
For the second run, Leclerc gave himself a bit of distance to his team-mate to not get caught out with a slow run down to Turn 1 to fire the tyres up.

His second preparation lap was much more aggressive – he ran into Turn 1 at more than 270km/h compared to around 230km/h when behind Hamilton. He was equally quicker through the first sequence of corners and up to Turn 4.

The preparation was clean and it seemed he had got the tyres well fired up for the start of the lap. He was 0.150 seconds up through the first sequence of corners, and a tenth up coming out of Turn 6.
But the lap fell away then as he lost a bunch of time between Turns 6 and 7 - suggesting the rears were getting hot and losing traction.

He regained a bit going super aggressive through the Turn 9/10/11 sequence, which triggered a slide, but that seemed to overheat his rubber even more – meaning all his advantage bled away from the stadium.
Leclerc knew he had blown it as he lambasted the “very shit lap” over the team radio afterwards, as well as the impact of a car that was “quite a bit different with a normal lap”.
He also suggested he was “really pissed “ with how things had been managed.
Speaking in the post-qualifying press conference, Leclerc did not make any further reference to what he was annoyed about – as he instead made clear he was more angry with himself.
“I just didn't do a good enough job,” he said. “Yes, tyre preparation is quite key. I kind of struggled to have the same conditions for my out-lap throughout the qualifying.
“But at the end of the day, when I had a clean out-lap in Q3, run two, I didn't do the job. So I can only be angry with myself.”

There was perhaps no better example of the gains that came from good preparation and perfect execution than George Russell, who baffled himself with a lap that came within 0.009 seconds of pole position to take second on the grid.
Russell has not felt comfortable with the upgraded Mercedes all weekend, and things had not looked good throughout early qualifying as his squad went for a double prep lap approach.
With that not working, Russell opted to switch tactics and go straight on the attack for his final run – and it unleashed pace that even he was at a loss to explain.
“It's a little bit of a story of my season,” he said. “I think this kind of feels like I've never done an average lap. It's either a terrible lap or a very strong lap, and this is quite frustrating.

“I don't think there was a single lap this whole weekend ahead of Q3 that I looked in the mix to even fight for the top three, let alone pole position. But that last lap just came together really nicely. I'd love to know exactly why, but I don't have those answers.”

It also left Russell rueing the smallest of details. Having been fuelled for a double prep lap, the Mercedes was carrying more load than needed – and that extra weight likely would have cost more than the 0.009 deficit he ended up losing pole by.
“You always think retrospectively, if only we had the one lap of fuel rather than the extra lap of fuel that we had, we could have been on pole,” he said.
As Hamilton showed in pulling off pole, such small details can be critical – even before the qualifying lap has even started.

items.originalTitle: Liam Lawson disqualified from F1 qualifying in Mexico – here's why
items.summaryEn: Liam Lawson has been disqualified from qualifying for the Mexico City Grand Prix due to a technical infringement concerning the MGU-K rampdown rate, costing him his ninth-place starting position.
detailZh: 利亚姆·劳森被取消墨西哥站F1排位赛成绩——原因如下
劳森因技术违规被排除在排位赛成绩之外。该问题涉及他在Q2完成最快圈后的MGU-K降速速率。
利亚姆·劳森失去了F1墨西哥城大奖赛第九位的发车位置。
小红牛周六在罗德里格斯兄弟赛道表现出色，两辆赛车均闯入Q3。车队随后以第八和第九位成为其余车队中的最佳，但劳森现在要在周日正赛中追赶。
这位新西兰车手因技术违规被国际汽联取消资格。传唤文件中已经写明：“劳森在Q2最快圈过线后不久，于15:47:36违反了MGU-K最低功率要求。”
在前往干事处后，结果与几乎所有技术违规相同：取消资格。实际上，劳森在完成Q2最快圈后没有立即松开油门，这意味着他未能遵守规定的MGU-K降功率速率。
根据技术规则第C5.12.6条，该电功率必须逐渐降低。该条规定每秒最大降低50或100千瓦：
“当ERS-K的直流电功率高于100千瓦时，车手最大功率需求的降低速率不得超过以下定义值：
a. 在国际汽联认定功率受限距离超过3500米的比赛中，任意1秒周期内为50千瓦。用于计算功率受限距离的车辆基础数据可在文件FIA-F1-DOC-034中查阅。
b. 在所有其他比赛中，任意1秒周期内为100千瓦。”
在劳森的情况下，正如赛事干事报告所述，他在越过终点线后未能立即松开油门，因此电功率的下降速率更为陡峭。
“提交的证据（所有在场各方均予接受）显示，在他Q2最快圈结束后的控制线之后，该车手并未立即松开动力。这导致实现规定‘降档’所需的MGU-K部署降低速率未能达成。”
传唤文件进一步说明了这一违规行为如下：“车手的最大功率需求和 ERS-K 的直流电功率以高于规则允许的速率被降低。”
在听证会上，各方均认定小红牛（小红牛）未从该违规中获得任何竞技优势，尽管这一认定不足以避免取消资格。毕竟，技术违规始终是非黑即白的。
“车队辩称这并未提供任何性能优势，但很明显，即使未获得性能优势，也不能免除不遵守技术规则的责任。此外，这些规则要求赛车在赛事期间必须始终符合规则。”
“干事特别指出，车队自行披露了违规行为，但有许多先例要求我们，尽管存在所有减轻情节，在赛车不符合技术规则时仍必须处以取消资格的处罚。”
这意味着劳森在周日将不得不从发车格最后一位起步，并面临一路超车追赶的局面。这次取消资格对阿尔派来说是好消息，其争夺车队积分榜第五名的对手之一如今被迫从最后一位起步。不过在积分榜上，小红牛仍以33分的优势稳居前列。
detailEn: Liam Lawson disqualified from F1 qualifying in Mexico – here's why
Lawson has been excluded from the qualifying results due to a technical infringement. It concerns the MGU-K rampdown rate after he completed his fastest lap in Q2
Liam Lawson has lost his ninth-place starting position for the Formula 1 Mexico City Grand Prix.

Racing Bulls impressed at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez on Saturday and managed to get both cars into Q3. The team subsequently emerged as the 'best of the rest' in eighth and ninth places, but Lawson now faces a recovery drive on Sunday.

The New Zealander has been disqualified by the FIA for a technical infringement. The summons document had already stated that “Lawson was in breach of the minimum MGU-K power requirement just after crossing the line on his fastest lap in Q2 at 15:47:36.”

Following a visit to the stewards, the outcome was the same as for almost all technical infringements: disqualification. In practice, Lawson did not immediately lift off the throttle after completing his fastest Q2 lap, meaning he failed to comply with the prescribed MGU-K rampdown rate.
That electrical power must be reduced gradually in accordance with Article C5.12.6 of the technical regulations. It stipulates maximum reductions of either 50 or 100kW per second:
“The driver maximum power demand must not be reduced at any greater than the rates defined below whilst the electrical DC power of the ERS-K is above 100kW:

a. 50kW in any 1s period at Competitions where the FIA determines that the power limited distance exceeds 3500m. The vehicle fundamentals used for the calculation of the power limited distance may be found in the document FIA-F1-DOC-034.
b. 100kW in any 1s period at all other Competitions.”
In Lawson's case, that rampdown rate of the electrical power was steeper after he failed to lift off the throttle immediately upon crossing the line, as described in the stewards' report.

“Evidence submitted, which was accepted by all parties present, showed that after the control line at the end of his fastest lap in Q2, the driver did not lift off the power immediately. This resulted in the rate of reduction of MGU-K deployment required to achieve the regulated “step down”, not being achieved.”

The summons document further clarified this breach as follows: “The driver maximum power demand and the electrical DC power of the ERS-K were reduced at greater rates than what is permitted by the Regulations.”

During the hearing, all parties concluded that Racing Bulls had gained no sporting advantage from the infringement, although that finding was not enough to prevent the disqualification. Technical infringements are, after all, always black and white.

“The team argued that this did not provide any performance advantage however it is clear that non-compliance with the Technical Regulations is not excused if no performance advantage is gained. Further, these regulations require that a car must comply with them at all times during an event.

“The Stewards note in particular that the team self-disclosed the breach however there are a multitude of precedents that require us, despite all mitigating circumstances, to impose a penalty of Disqualfication where a car does not comply with the Technical Regulations.”

It means Lawson will have to start from the very back of the grid on Sunday and faces a fight through the field. The disqualification is good news for Alpine, with one of its rivals for fifth place in the constructors' championship now forced to start from the back. In the standings, however, Racing Bulls still holds a comfortable 33-point advantage.
keyPointsZh: 违规涉及他在Q2完成最快圈后的MGU-K降速速率
小红牛两车均进入Q3，原本占据第八和第九位，为其余车队中最佳
劳森周日正赛将从后方起步追赶
keyPointsEn: The infringement concerns the MGU-K rampdown rate after he completed his fastest lap in Q2.
Racing Bulls got both cars into Q3 and were the best of the rest in eighth and ninth.
Lawson now faces a recovery drive in Sunday's race.
